name: Parsley
frostTenderNotes: Not stated directly by the sourced KZN DARD documents. Parsley is sown across the 'Cold areas / Moderate frosts' window (Aug-Mar) per Table 6, and EcoCrop's KTMP (killing temperature) of 0°C for Petroselinum crispum suggests only light frost tolerance, but no SA source gives an explicit statement, so left null.

transplant.notes: Parsley is not named in the document's list of crops that 'transplant comparatively easily', and Table 5 gives it only a Direct-sow rate with no Seedtray/Seedbed figures — the same pattern shown for other direct-sown crops (radish, parsnip) in that table.

daysToHarvestRange.notes: KZN's 70-80 day figure is the primary source, corroborated exactly by the Starke Ayres 'Parsley Plain' cultivar. A second catalogue entry on the same page, printed as 'DAYS TO MATURITY: 12-14' next to 'PARSLEY MOSS CURLED', is almost certainly a PDF-layout extraction artefact (a curly parsley cultivar reaching full maturity in 12-14 days is agronomically implausible and inconsistent with every other parsley source found) and was not used.

varietiesNotes: Zones are the catalogue's own generic 'grows in all seasons' claim applied broadly, since the source does not name specific SA regions; karoo-arid and high-mountain are left out as this claim and the KZN sowing table do not address those extreme-climate zones.

zoneNotes.highveld: KZN's 'Cold areas / Moderate frosts' window (Aug-Mar) applies per the sourced 3-tier table.
zoneNotes.lowveld-bushveld: Falls under 'Hot areas / Frost-free' (Feb-Sept) per the sourced table.
zoneNotes.subtropical-coast: Falls under 'Hot areas / Frost-free' (Feb-Sept); not separately confirmed.
zoneNotes.midlands-mistbelt: KZN's own 'Warm areas / Light frosts' window (Jul-Apr, nearly year-round) applies directly.
zoneNotes.western-cape: Not covered by a Western Cape-specific source; 'winter' sowMonths inferred equal to 'summer' — flagged gap.
zoneNotes.karoo-arid: Not confirmed by source; EcoCrop's TMAX of 28°C suggests some heat sensitivity that could be a concern in this zone's summer extremes.
zoneNotes.high-mountain: Not confirmed by source; EcoCrop's KTMP of 0°C suggests limited frost tolerance, a concern in a severe-frost zone.

gaps: No Western Cape/winter-rainfall-specific sowing calendar found; 'winter' sowMonths inferred equal to 'summer'.
frostTender left null — no explicit cold-tolerance statement found; EcoCrop's KTMP=0°C is the only climate signal available.
One Starke Ayres catalogue entry ('Parsley Moss Curled') has an implausible printed days-to-maturity figure (12-14 days), judged a PDF-extraction artefact and left out rather than recorded as fact.
No DAFF or provincial government (rather than seed-catalogue) source for named parsley cultivars was found.
summary: Sourced from three KZN DARD 'Vegetable Production Guidelines' chapters (Plant Establishment, Length of Growing Period, Expected Yields) plus a Starke Ayres home-garden catalogue for varieties. SowMonths (all four columns), row/in-row spacing, sow depth, seed rate, days-to-harvest (70-80 days) and yield (2-4 t/ha) are all directly quoted and cross-validated between the KZN and seed-catalogue sources. Remaining gaps are a Western Cape-specific sowing calendar and an explicit frost-tolerance statement.
